clue.text: Renegade, with silver hidden in dam, forms an elaborate plan

indicators.note: something hidden in a place sits inside it, so the first pieces go inside the word for dam

parts.note: to dam a flow is to stem it
a rat is a deserter or turncoat
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A traitor stashes stolen silver inside a dam as part of an intricate scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' looks like a noun for a barrier, but here it is the verb meaning to hold back a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme or ruse devised to outwit someone.

clue.text: Whacks with items of clothing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hits hard, as a verb
second meaning: garments worn on the feet

explanation.surface: Someone lashes out using pieces of clothing as weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an informal verb for punching someone and the plural noun for foot garments.

clue.text: Managed to get rid of plunder

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
to sack is to dismiss from a job

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in disposing of their loot.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search a place violently and steal from it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: During winter, sex is brief!

indicators.note: something occurring during a span lies within it, so the letters sit inside the run of words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A cheeky observation that cold-weather lovemaking is short-lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means short and to the point, an adjective synonym of brief.

clue.text: Sticky stuff decays in treats

parts.note: goo is any sticky substance
something that decays slowly dies away

explanation.surface: A gooey substance is rotting inside some sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodies are nice things to eat or receive, the same as treats.

clue.text: Worried aunt got me a vegetable

indicators.note: a worried thing is agitated and churned about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An anxious aunt has bought someone a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: A mangetout is the flat edible-podded pea, called a snow pea in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout is a type of pea eaten pod and all, so it is a vegetable.

clue.text: Lecherous look of king reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch

explanation.surface: A news item about a monarch eyeing someone lustfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, suggestive glance expressing sexual desire.

clue.text: Young mammal always restricted by obstruction

indicators.note: something restricted by another is hemmed in by it, so it goes inside

parts.note: a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance', and in tennis
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A young animal is perpetually hemmed in by some barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year, so a young mammal.

clue.text: Evangelical Union against the Messiah embracing a sacrament

parts.note: initials of the two words

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap the arms around, so one piece holds the next inside

parts.note: Christ is the Messiah in Christian belief
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church body opposing Christ over a holy rite sounds like a doctrinal row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' looks like opposition, but it only means placed beside, as one thing leans against another.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist, or Holy Communion, is one of the Christian sacraments.

clue.text: I censor a badly written summary of play's plot

indicators.note: writing done badly leaves letters out of their proper order

parts.note: eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A censor confesses to cutting a poorly written theatre synopsis.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of the plot of a play or film, scene by scene.

clue.text: No sin found in one yet to take vows

parts.note: taken as written
a vice is a sinful habit

explanation.surface: A trainee nun or monk is blameless so far.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a probationer in a religious order who has not yet taken final vows.

clue.text: Invest a tenner to secure property

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within, so the words grip the letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: Advice to put ten pounds into buying land or a house.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is landed property, or a person's total assets.

clue.text: I cry loudly for dessert

parts.note: to cry loudly is to scream; said aloud, 'I scream' matches the dessert

explanation.surface: Someone wails to get a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate sound signal: 'loudly' both makes cry into scream and hints at speech, echoing the rhyme 'I scream, you scream'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is a frozen sweet served as a pudding course.

clue.text: Nonsense talked in bed leading to expression of doubt

parts.note: a bunk is a narrow bed
um is a hesitant noise of uncertainty

explanation.surface: Someone mumbling rubbish while lying in bed, then pausing doubtfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunkum is empty, foolish talk, a synonym of claptrap or rubbish.

clue.text: Girl out, so arranged for a physician

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A girl is away, so a doctor has been booked instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A urologist is a medical specialist in the urinary tract, a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Must opera turn into long-running play?

indicators.note: to turn into something is to be transformed, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether an opera has to be converted into a stage hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap is Agatha Christie's murder mystery, running in London's West End since 1952.
explanation.definitionFit: Christie's play holds the record for the longest continuous run of any stage show.

clue.text: Drink in Soho, having time to get wasted

indicators.note: wasted letters are smashed up like a drunk, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boozy night out in London's Soho district, taking time to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' and 'wasted' suggest alcohol, but the answer is a blended fruit drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothie is a thick blended beverage of fruit, yoghurt or milk.

clue.text: Bone discovered in barrow is about to perish

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a barrow is an ancient burial mound
a rib is a bone of the chest

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds a bone in a burial site belonging to someone near death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrow' suggests a wheelbarrow, but here it is a prehistoric grave mound.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund means at the point of death, or in terminal decline.

clue.text: Refused to have anything to with editor after groin trouble

definitions.text: Refused to have anything to with

indicators.note: after places the editor's abbreviation second, behind the reworked body part
trouble stirs things up and leaves them disordered, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: five letters to rearrange
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone shunned the editor after a groin injury.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has dropped a word: it should read 'Refused to have anything to do with'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to pay them no attention, refusing any dealings with them.

clue.text: Dickens' first twenty quires given to Queen by idealist

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the name is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the novelist's name
a ream is a paper measure of twenty quires
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Dickens's opening batch of paper handed to the monarch by a visionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer is someone with impractical, idealistic notions, so an idealist.

clue.text: Tea ordered in attempt to reach agreement between states

indicators.note: things ordered are put into a fresh sequence, so these letters are rearranged
placed in another word, the rearranged letters sit inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
the letters of tea rearranged

explanation.surface: Diplomats call for tea while trying to hammer out a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal pact concluded between nations.

clue.text: Former Liberal issues a warning

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
liberal in the sense of generous or plentiful

explanation.surface: A one-time Liberal Party politician sounds a note of caution.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes Liberal look like a party member; it is the adjective meaning generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone punished to deter others is made an example, a warning to the rest.

clue.text: Stick together where the money is?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be united in one substance or whole
second, playful meaning: split into two words, it points to the place cash is kept

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey second reading, which splits the answer into a phrase about cash being here.
explanation.definitionFit: Coinhere is a rare verb meaning to exist together in one thing, close to cohering or adhering.

clue.text: State adopting dancing bear is not far away

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places
to adopt is to take in, so the state's letters hold the others

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York state
the letters of bear rearranged

explanation.surface: A US state that takes in a performing bear lies close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby means close at hand, within a short distance.

clue.text: Nick's not at church

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A man called Nick has skipped the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick reads as a name; it is the lower-case word for a small cut, and the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut, the same thing as a nick.

clue.text: Promote footwear worn by Scottish leader

indicators.note: footwear is worn around the foot, so the shoe word wraps the other letter

parts.note: a boot is a kind of footwear

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter, so just the start is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Advertising a shoe brand worn by Scotland's First Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost something is to promote or publicise it to increase its standing.

clue.text: Surrealist painter claiming right to meet central character in Carroll's Looking Glass

indicators.note: claiming something means taking it in, so the painter's name holds the next letter

parts.note: Joan Miró was a Spanish surrealist
R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: the central character is the one in the middle of the word

parts.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter name

explanation.surface: A surrealist artist meets Lewis Carroll's heroine in his Through the Looking-Glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central character' sounds like Alice, but it means the middle letter of Carroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking glass is an old-fashioned name for a mirror.

clue.text: "All the world's a stage" is one trope ham delivered badly

definitions.text: "All the world's a stage" is one

indicators.note: lines delivered badly come out jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A hammy actor mangles Jaques's famous line from As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line describes life as theatre without 'like' or 'as', which makes it a metaphor rather than a simile.

clue.text: Boss of a breeding establishment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a raised knob or ornamental ... on a surface
second meaning: a farm where horses are kept for breeding

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' reads as the person in charge, but it is a projecting knob, as on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is both a decorative raised boss and a place keeping stallions for breeding.

clue.text: Priest leading men to evangelist's final manuscript

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for priest
arch means chief, as in arch-rival
taken as written

indicators.note: the final of a word is its closing letter, so only the end is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cleric guides his flock towards an evangelist's last written document.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment is prepared animal skin for writing on, and by extension a manuscript written on it.
